task.title: EACQ-FV L3 Automation-Assist Owner Drift Reconciliation
task.objective: Restore the automation-assist focused suite by reconciling PathPlan constructor drift and packet-shape vocabulary ownership without weakening the L2 semantic diagnostic.
nonGoals: Do not change dispatch-quality, worker-return, commit-steward, autorun, scaffold, template, registry, or session owners.
Do not remove or weaken required or conditional packet-shape diagnostics introduced into generated work orders by L2.
Do not create a new contract vocabulary, checker, helper, or test file.
Do not commit, stage, push, publish, deploy, call providers, or use credentials.

gateA.name: SOURCE_OWNER_OVERLAP
requiredEvidence: Reproduce the 53/82 focused-suite failures and classify all of them before editing.
Confirm 51 failures come from the test helper omitting mixed_atomicity_authorized and two come from deleted dispatch-quality constant attributes.
Confirm the compact dispatch profile and detailed worker-return headings have different current owners.
Confirm the automation-assist semantic vocabulary remains useful to L2 and must not be weakened.

gateB.name: DESIGN_CODE_TEST
requiredEvidence: Change only the automation-assist helper, its existing focused test file, and the named worker return.
Repair the PathPlan test factory with the current constructor field and preserve default non-mixed behavior.
Replace stale owner-mirroring claims and tests with truthful current-owner boundaries while retaining semantic diagnostics.
Keep net line delta at or below zero for both exception-registry-owned Python files.
Run the complete focused suite, size guard, pre-implementation gate, and worker-return fast gate.

competingOwnersChecked: Dispatch-quality owns the compact dispatch profile; worker-return quality owns detailed return headings; this helper owns only early advisory semantic diagnostics.
The PathPlan production owner remains read-only; only the stale automation-assist test factory is repaired.
Detailed worker-return headings are current machine authority but do not include every work-order-side contextual instruction.
This checker owns compact dispatch-profile terms and the shared section marker, not the deleted detailed semantic tuples.

freshness.anchor: L2 accepted material plus the reproduced L3 failure taxonomy
freshness.regenerateWhen: packet-shape diagnostics or PathPlan constructor changes

mustPreserve: Preserve all required and conditional semantic diagnostics and N/A-with-reason handling used by L2 generated work orders.
Keep compact dispatch-profile enforcement distinct from detailed return-heading enforcement and advisory work-order diagnostics.
Keep both exception-registry-owned Python files at or below their current line counts: 1318 and 1289.
Keep runtime, commit-steward, checker, scaffold, template, and public/provider behavior unchanged.
forbiddenTransitions: Do not make the helper import the heavy dispatch-quality checker merely to recreate deleted constants.
Do not delete semantic terms to make stale drift tests pass.
Do not edit the exception registry or increase either approved line count.
Do not stage or commit worker changes.

freshness.anchor: final unstaged worker diff against execution base
freshness.regenerateWhen: any helper, test, or worker-return line changes after verification

negativeCases: Any remaining TypeError caused by omitted mixed_atomicity_authorized fails.
Any test or comment still claiming deleted detailed tuples are mirrored from dispatch-quality fails.
Any loss of a required or conditional semantic diagnostic term fails.
Any net line-count growth in either modified Python file fails.
Any changed path outside the exact helper/test/return manifest fails.
deterministicChecks: The test PathPlan factory explicitly sets mixed_atomicity_authorized=False.
The section marker remains aligned with its current dispatch-quality owner.
Detailed headings are checked only against a current truthful owner or explicit local advisory contract.
